gaps: ChessLab's generic Receipt type (contract.ts:127-141) carries no value field at all — declaredConsumes/actualConsumes/actualProduces/writes are address strings and write-kind labels, never the Part's actual content; the only place a learner sees an actual computed value (piece list, candidate score, check witness) is debugger.ts's hand-assembled snapshot.observed/policy, which is bespoke per-cartridge code, not something the shared host.ts/board.ts/contract.ts machinery gives for free to a new domain.

ChessLab's declared-vs-actual conformance (accessConformance:'exact', cartridge.ts:6,15-16; enforced host.ts:22-27) is a silent pass / fatal-crash gate, not a rendered comparison panel — a learner only ever sees the raw declaredConsumes/actualConsumes arrays side by side inside a JSON dump ('run'/'receipt') and must diff them by eye; there is no UI that highlights the delta.

ChessLab has two structurally different 'receipt' commands reachable from the same CLI: the S0/S1 cartridge path (host.ts, exact-conformance-checked, calculation-hash-frozen) versus the King/Queen Study path (state.ts session, no OperationSpec, no conformance check, no calculation hash) — a learner typing 'receipt' in Study mode is getting materially weaker testimony than 'receipt'/'run' in debugger mode, with no signal in the UI that the two are different guarantees.

ChessLab's default learner-facing view named by the README ('inspect both sides' -> 'mind'/'why') shows only outcomes (candidates, scores, witnesses) and never shows a Tick or a Calculation identity — recovering 'what the algorithm used' still requires a separate, differently-formatted raw-JSON command ('run'), which is exactly the gap origin.md says PxC was built to close; it is closed for an agent reading JSON, not yet for the learner using the named debugger.

ChessLab's replayView.ts historical game replay runs no Calculations at all (lab/replay.ts is a pure frame cursor) — for that mode there is nothing to show; the 'run'/'mind' commands are the only way to get any Tick, and they operate on the live current replay frame, not the historical frame's own game context.

Wumpus's interactive TUI '--inspect' panel is fed a snapshot that deliberately deletes inputs/outputs/result and reduces calculations to bare addresses (session.js:26-29) even though execute.js computed and froze the full values moments earlier (execute.js:22-37) — the richest part of the receipt is thrown away before it reaches the only always-available human view, and only the last 3 ticks survive per frame.

Full per-Tick values in Wumpus are recoverable only via --save-to-file (opened outside the TUI) or the browser-workbench's traceAddress click-through (one node's value at a time, arrays over 40 entries truncated by compact()) — there is no view that shows a full Tick's complete inputs/outputs together in one place for a human, only piecewise or file-based access.

Wumpus's constraint evaluator computes and returns exactly which addresses it read and which were missing (constraint.js reads/missing), i.e. its own declared-vs-actual-read testimony, but the only UI consuming it (browser-workbench.js:46) discards reads/missing/measurements and shows just a status word and a prose reason.

Wumpus's own failure-profile research experiment runs named PxC Ticks over the profiling oracle but strips the records before publishing results.json/README — even the project's internal use of the engine for a written finding does not carry the Tick trace into the artifact a reader sees.

Neither runtime has a UI that lets a person browse 'every historical value an address held, across every Tick that touched it' — Wumpus's traceAddress can do this programmatically for a given end record set, but no rendered view exposes it as a scrollable/browsable history; ChessLab cannot do it even programmatically because addresses are never versioned or value-captured in receipts.

docs/core.md:20 states outright that Wumpus's provenance/composition metadata 'does not grant access to engine internals and is not required for ordinary world execution' — the origin need (seeing what the algorithm used) is explicitly framed there as optional/descriptive rather than load-bearing, which is a documented design position, not an oversight, but it does mean the founding need is only met when a caller opts in (--inspect, --save, or the workbench), not by default.
agent_annotation_surface: For an agent (not a human UI), the two runtimes offer very different surfaces to read/write Tick material. Wumpus: `investigate(frame).records`, `session.records`, and `session.export()` (session.js:46,55; investigation.js:13-36) are plain JSON-serializable arrays where every record already carries full `inputs`, `outputs`, and per-calculation `input`/`output` values (execute.js:22-37, pxc.js:26-69 captureValue), and `traceAddress(records, address)` (provenance.js:41-80) walks producer chains over that same array to build a value-annotated lineage tree — an agent gets complete, generically-addressable Part values with zero extra instrumentation, the same data structure whether it's coming from a play session, the investigation module, or the failure-profile oracle. ChessLab: `runDebugger(frame, variant).ticks` (Receipt[], contract.ts:127-141) is also JSON-serializable and carries declared/actual address sets, write-kind testimony, and frozen-calculation identity hashes, but it carries no Part values at all; an agent wanting a value at a given address must separately call `host.px.get(address)` on the live PxC board while it is still in scope (board.ts:56-64) — there is no snapshot/versioning, so a later Tick's write silently overwrites what an earlier Tick's receipt referred to, with no record of the prior value anywhere. The one place ChessLab values do reach an agent-readable structure is debugger.ts's `snapshot.observed`/`policy` (debugger.ts:56-69), but that is bespoke composition code written once for the chess cartridge; a new cartridge author would have to hand-write an equivalent composition step to get any value-observability at all, whereas in Wumpus every cartridge/domain gets full-value receipts for free from executeTick itself.

runtime: Two runtimes were inspected, both against the PCR -> Tick[] -> Calculation[] shape from pyto/research/origin.md:20-23 ("Each Tick is where its Calculations become observable"). (1) DiscStudio browser app: src/app.js (UI), src/runtime.js (adapter that builds Tick[]/Calculation[] via `step()` and executes via PQL), src/core/exec.js (readPql/invokePql/trackAccess), src/review.js + public/tick-part-checklist.js + src/review-data.js (review overlay), README.md (Integration contract / Review sections). (2) pyto Python library: pyto/src/pyto/pcr.py (PCR/Tick/Invocation, PcrRun testimony+receipts, mermaid()), pyto/src/pyto/core.py (Part/Calculation/PxC), pyto/src/pyto/neon.py (pixel-level materialization helpers), and three experiment trees that each write their own evidence files on top of that library: pyto/experiments/grouped-ablation/evidence/* (testimony.json, receipts.json, retained.json, comparison.md/json, mermaid.mmd), pyto/experiments/art-tournament/{harness,renders,studios} (rendered SVG/PNG + pcr-testimony.json + contact sheets), pyto/experiments/runs/day1/verdicts/*.json (test-verification lenses, not execution traces). Across both runtimes the generic trace/testimony/receipt machinery is address- and hash-only; wherever an actual computed value becomes human-visible without running code, it is because one specific screen (DiscStudio's "Inspect Part" click) or one specific experiment script (grouped-ablation's comparison.md, art-tournament's rendered PNGs) chose to surface it, not because the PCR/PxC contract does.

gaps: DiscStudio's on-screen trace table drops the Tick name: runtime.js:55 attaches `tick: t.name` to every trace row, but app.js's tracePanel() never reads `.tick` (verified: no `t.tick` reference exists anywhere in src/app.js) — a person watching the live UI sees which fn.* Calculation ran, not which named step ('Fields:discId', 'ArrangeComparison', ...) it belongs to, even though DiscStudio's own step() helper makes Tick and Calculation 1:1 so the name would be free to show.

DiscStudio's trace/receipt objects never carry resolved Part values, even though invokePql (src/core/exec.js:47) computes them in memory as `inputs`/`output` per calculation — runtime.js:55 explicitly re-extracts the address forms (c.with, c.into) instead, so neither the on-screen table nor the downloadable receipt (trace-export) ever embeds a value.

DiscStudio's only value-bearing view ('Inspect Part') is reachable solely for Parts that currently appear as an `output` button in the open trace table; the exhaustive Part index (src/app.js:133, runtime.parts()) lists every address ever set but has no click-through, so most of the PxC store is unreachable from the UI without opening the browser console and using window.discStudio.runtime.pxc.get(address) directly (src/app.js:393) — i.e. still requires writing code.

pyto's generic PCR/retain/testimony/receipt machinery is value-blind by explicit design: retained.json's 'results' are literally {invocation id: sha256|None} (pyto/experiments/grouped-ablation/retain.py:28, confirmed against evidence/run-1/retained.json), and Receipt.result_sha256 (pcr.py:125) is a one-way digest. There is no generic pyto file or command that lets a person see what a Tick's Calculations actually computed without writing and running Python to call pxc.get(address) or PCR.run(...).results themselves.

The one place pyto surfaces an actual computed value in readable form (comparison.md/json in grouped-ablation) exists only because that experiment's run.py hand-wrote a report from the in-memory Python result, bypassing testimony/receipts/retained entirely; it covers only the terminal 'Compare' Tick. No equivalent readable dump exists anywhere in the evidence tree for the 'Fit' or 'Score' Ticks that fed it — their values are hash-only.

The art-tournament renders make final Part values visible as literal pixels (the strongest 'pixels retained' evidence found in either runtime), but no file in that tree links a specific rendered filename to the Part address or invocation id that produced it — pcr-testimony.json carries the addresses, the PNG/SVG files carry the pixels, and nothing observed ties the two together by address (studios/botanical/manifest.json was checked and contains design prose, not a filename-to-address map).

Neither runtime's annotation surface is scoped to a PCR Tick/Calculation/Part identity: DiscStudio's neat-review checklist (src/review-data.js) keys comments to a fixed, hand-authored list of feature-review topics ('domain', 'trace', 'feedback', ...), not to any runtime Tick name or fn.* address; pyto's closest analogue (runs/day1 verdict findings) keys its notes to source line numbers ('pcr.py:45'), not to Tick/Calculation/invocation ids, even though testimony.json/mermaid.mmd/receipts.json already assign exactly those stable ids. This reproduces, inside the current tooling, the origin.md complaint that 'agents had to annotate, and the annotations carried no meaning' (origin.md:11-12).
agent_annotation_surface: No surface examined lets a human or agent attach a comment scoped to the PCR's own Tick/Calculation/Part identity, despite that identity existing and being fully computed in both runtimes. DiscStudio's real annotation surface is the neat-review checklist (src/review.js, src/review-data.js, public/tick-part-checklist.js): comments are keyed to fixed reviewIds from a hand-authored feature list ('identity','bags','trace','feedback',...) plus a captured UI context snapshot (route/discId/presetId/nodeId/stateId/worldLabel — src/app.js:181), not to any runtime Tick name or fn.* address; the actual PQL structure that DOES carry Tick names and addresses ('Inspect PQL composition', src/app.js:133) has no comment affordance attached to it at all. pyto's closest analogue is the runs/day1/verdicts findings and grouped-ablation's OPEN-FINDINGS.md, which anchor notes to source line numbers ('pcr.py:45', 'pql.py:73') or to whole evidence file paths, never to a Tick name or invocation id even though testimony.json/mermaid.mmd/receipts.json already assign exactly those stable, addressable ids per Calculation. The art-tournament contact_sheet.py grid overlay (harness/contact_sheet.py:9-11,23-40) is the one artifact literally built for annotation ('so judges can reference exact positions when leaving notes'), but it annotates pixel coordinates in a rendered image, not a Tick/Calculation/Part identity. Net: an agent today has three disconnected ways to leave a note (a fixed checklist id, a source line number, or an image pixel coordinate), and none of them is 'this Tick's this Calculation wrote this Part' — the identity scheme origin.md treats as the fix is present in the data (testimony.json ids, mermaid.mmd subgraphs, PQL composition Tick names) but has no comment box wired to it in either runtime.
